Finding a Company and the Report Types
Searching on Codal
Type the ticker or company name in the search box and pick it from the list. Watch out for rights tickers (suffix “ح”) and similar tickers.
Advanced search: announcement type, date range, audited/unaudited, consolidated/separate (check the exact filter names on the site; please check).
Each announcement has a web version, a PDF and sometimes an Excel file. Take numbers from Excel or the web tables; notes and the auditor’s report usually from the PDF.
A “correction” means the previous version had an error; repeated corrections are a sign of disclosure quality.
The publication date and time matter: publishing late, or only on the last day of the deadline with bad numbers, is a pattern for some issuers.

Cash Flow and Equity
Cash flow: operating cash flow (CFO), purchases of fixed assets (CAPEX), dividends paid, borrowings.
If net profit is high but operating cash flow has been below it for years, the profit is stuck in receivables or inventory.

Qualified Opinions Are Common in Iran
Read the qualification items one by one: insufficient tax provision, old receivables, obsolete inventory, guarantees.
What matters is the amount and nature of the items, not just that they exist.
Difference from IFRS
Reporting under Iranian accounting standards (issued by the Audit Organization); some large companies also publish an IFRS version (check the scope).
No inflation adjustment.
Revaluation with a tax incentive, followed by a capital increase.
“Separate” and “consolidated” statements side by side; the Iranian market focuses mostly on the separate ones.
Duties of a Listed Company
From his note in Bahman 1398 (February 2020) (the rules may have changed; please check):
Financial statements with the auditor’s report, at the time of public release and within the disclosure deadline.
A loss-making year: the reasons for the loss and the plan ahead within 15 days of the auditor’s report.
Expansion projects: a progress report every 6 months (cost, percent complete, funding, start-up date, effect on profit).
An “adverse” opinion or a “disclaimer”: the ticker is halted until the issues are resolved.
Covered by Article 141 (accumulated losses above half the capital): if it doesn’t get out within a year, the stock goes to the unofficial board.
The auditor’s opinion increases the credibility of the financial statements.
